conviction_note: Near non-result. The quarter's swing lines are partly offsetting. On the negative side: a macro mortgage headwind (MBA 30-year rate rose from 6.65% in July to 7.12% in September; FB Financial's mortgage income fell 16% q/q), a fee cut the company itself flagged, and four Q2 CRE downgrades. On the positive side: a margin tailwind (Q2 NIM +11bp on securities repricing, 75bp cost of funds, one extra day, Fed hike on 9-16). Against a $0.94 bar that already sits a cent below Q2 and $0.04 above Q4, that nets to a slight miss lean at most. p_up 46 times abs_move 3.0 gives -0.24. The findings sum to +0.10, because the beat-rate base rate (9 of 11) offsets the proxies; the two numbers differ in sign but both are within noise of zero.
bar: Q3 2026 diluted EPS consensus $0.94 (Benzinga https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CCBG/earnings-forecasts, Stockalarm https://pro.stockalarm.io/quote/CCBG/earnings: $0.94, revenue $66M), Earnings Whispers $0.95 (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/CCBG). Two sources agree at $0.94. The sweep row says n_estimates is 1, so the bar is soft. Q4'26E is $0.90, which suggests the fee reduction is modelled. There is no company guidance beyond a ~23.5% annual tax rate and a qualitative statement that deposit fees will fall from Q3 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000726601/000072660126000020/ex991.htm).
positioning_check: Short interest is 567.9K shares, 3.3% of float, 6.6 days to cover, falling 6% month over month (Equibles 'latest settlement', page short-volume data as of 2026-10-16, https://equibles.com/stocks/CCBG). The high days-to-cover reflects thin volume (78K shares/day), not a crowded short. There is no usable option chain (empty_chain), so there is no skew. Run-up is -2.59% over 20 days and +1.03% over 5 days, 7.5% below the 52-week high. The market has made no directional statement.

findings.finding: Mortgage rates rose through Q3 2026: MBA conforming 30-year fixed was 6.65% in mid-July, 6.79% in late August and 7.12% in the week to Sep 18 (highest since May 2024), with applications down 4.1%, 1.5% and 6% in successive September weeks. CCBG's mortgage banking revenue (Q2 $4.66M, Q3'25 $4.79M, Q4'25 $4.16M) is its most rate-sensitive fee line. A $0.4-0.9M q/q decline costs about $0.02-0.04 EPS against a $0.94 bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 mortgage revenue rose $0.4M q/q on higher production, part of the noninterest-income beat behind a $0.95 vs $0.90 beat and +3.81% on the day. There is no clean record of a mortgage-led miss.
findings.why_not_priced: A one-analyst bank's estimate of $0.94 is barely below Q2's $0.95, and that gap is more easily explained by the flagged deposit-fee cut than by a mortgage slowdown. If the analyst had modelled both, the bar would sit nearer $0.92. Nobody previews CCBG's mortgage line.
findings.independence: Peer: FB Financial (Southeast bank with a large mortgage arm) reported Q3 2026 mortgage banking income of $9.4M vs $11.2M in Q2, -16%, on Oct 13 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001649749/000164974926000063/a3q26pressreleasetablesfor.htm). Regions' mortgage income fell 3% q/q (https://finviz.com/news/403470/regions-reports-earnings-of-611-million-and-eps-of-071-in-3q-2026). Both are macro and peer proxies; CCBG has not confirmed anything.

findings.finding: Margin tailwind into Q3. Q2 NIM rose 11bp to 4.35% on higher securities yields and lower deposit costs (cost of funds down 6bp to 75bp), and tax-equivalent NII was $44.2M. Q3 has one more day than Q2, securities keep repricing, and the Fed raised rates 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, which a low-cost-deposit bank absorbs better than peers. NII up $0.5-1.0M q/q would add about $0.02-0.045 EPS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: NIM +11bp and a $0.05 EPS beat, stock +3.81%. Jan 2026 print: -5.17% (cause not established here).
findings.why_not_priced: The Q2 trend is public, but a $0.94 bar below Q2's $0.95 implies the analyst expects no further NII growth. If continued expansion were in the price, the bar would sit at or above Q2.
findings.independence: Mixed peer read: Regions NIM +2bp q/q on fixed-rate asset turnover (https://finviz.com/news/403470/regions-reports-earnings-of-611-million-and-eps-of-071-in-3q-2026), while FB Financial NIM fell 12bp on higher deposit costs (FBK release above). The Fed hike is from https://investinglive.com/central-banks/fomc-rate-decision-fed-hikes-for-the-first-time-in-three-years/ (secondary source).

findings.finding: The company said in the Q2 release that it is 'reviewing and updating our deposit product offerings' and expects the modifications 'will reduce related fee revenues beginning in the third quarter of 2026'. It gave no amount. Q2 deposit fees were $5.66M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the first quarter of the change, so there is no history on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the company told the market, and the Q3 bar of $0.94 sits below Q2 while Q4E is $0.90. Only the size is unknown. A cut of $0.5M per quarter or more could exceed what one analyst modelled, and a smaller one could beat it.
findings.independence: Same document as the margin finding (the Q2 release), but a different line. No independent source.

findings.finding: In Q2 2026, classified loans rose $15.3M to $29.8M on downgrades of four CRE relationships: two private schools ($6.4M and $3.4M), a hotel ($2.0M) and a funeral home ($5.0M). NPAs were $13.4M and NCOs 14bp. A Q3 charge-off or specific reserve on any of these would raise provision above Q2's $0.9M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on file for a credit-led reaction at CCBG. Credit has been benign, with Q1 NCOs at 10bp.
findings.why_not_priced: Disclosed in July, so this is largely public. What is not priced is resolution: one analyst models provision as a run-rate. A $2-3M reserve on a $9.8M school exposure would cost about $0.10 EPS and would show as a miss.
findings.independence: Same Q2 release as findings 2 and 3, on a different line. No later document points either way. Regions' criticized loans fell q/q, a weak peer read the other way.

findings.finding: Beat base rate on a soft, single-analyst bar: CCBG beat EPS in 9 of its last 11 reports, and the Q2 2026 $0.95 came in against a $0.90 estimate. Five of the last seven prints closed up (median |move| 2.02%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat of $0.05 brought +3.81%. The prints of 2025-01 through 2025-10 were all small positives (+1.28 to +2.33%). 2026-01 was -5.17% and 2026-04 was -1.41%.
findings.why_not_priced: A conservative single estimate is a habit, not news. It is partly priced, and it is filed because it is the counterweight to the three negative proxies on a name with no skew to read.
findings.independence: Benzinga shows the same Q2 $0.95 vs $0.90 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CCBG/earnings-forecasts). The baseline's reaction history (5 of 7 up) is a separate dataset.

baseline_tension: There is no skew and the run-up is flat to slightly negative, so the baseline makes no directional statement for the evidence to agree or disagree with. The evidence itself nets near zero with a faint mortgage/fee-driven miss lean.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (inside what the company already told the market): the deposit-fee reduction finding moved from -0.2 to -0.1, because the company pre-announced it and the bar appears to embed it.
Lesson 5 (proxy, macro-to-company transmission not confirmed by the company): the mortgage finding moved from -0.4 to -0.3. It stays filed, with independence naming it a proxy.
Pessimism-artefact note: p_up moved from 45 to 46. abs_move stays at 3.0, above the 2.02 median, per the understatement lesson.
Left standing: the margin, credit and beat-base-rate findings. Lesson 8 does not apply because there is no confirmed, unpriced company-level number.
